chapters.title: Product Reviews
chapters.subtitle: Let buyers rate what they bought, and approve what shows

steps.text: Shoppers trust other shoppers. This video shows how product reviews work: what buyers see and write, how you approve each review, the settings that control them, and how ratings help shoppers find the best products.
Before they buy, shoppers look for proof that a product is good, and the best proof is what other buyers say.
A review you do not control can be a risk: spam, abuse, or a complaint about something you do not sell.
So every review is a rating from one to five stars, written by a customer, and approved by you before it shows.
The ratings then follow the product: stars on its page, and an average rating that shoppers can sort and filter your listings by.
A signed-in customer writes a review at the bottom of a product's page: stars, a title, a few words, and up to three photos.
When the customer bought the product, the review is marked Verified purchase.
A new or changed review waits under Commerce, Reviews until you approve it or reject it.
Approved reviews show on the product page and count toward its average, which your listings can filter and sort by.
Under a product's price, its stars, its average rating and its number of reviews link down to the reviews.
At the bottom of the page, Customer reviews shows the average and the approved reviews, newest first, each with its stars, title, author and date.

A signed-in customer sees Write a review under the reviews. A visitor who is not signed in is asked to sign in, and when your settings allow only buyers to review, a customer who has not bought the product is told so.
Let's write a review as a customer. Choose Your rating, from one to five stars.
Add a Title, and write Your review in a few words about what they liked or did not like. Both are optional, but they help other shoppers decide.
Check the Name shown with your review. It is filled in for the customer, and they can change it.
Click Send review. The customer is told that the review will show once you approve it. They can change it later, and a changed review waits for approval again.
Open Commerce, Reviews. It lists the reviews waiting for approval, newest first, with the product, the author, the rating, the title and text, and whether it is a verified purchase.
Click Approve to show a review on its product page, and to count it in the product's average rating.
Click Reject to keep a review off the product, such as this one, which is spam.
The list beside the count filters by status: Waiting for approval, Approved, Rejected or Any status. You can change your mind about any review.
Delete removes a review for good.
Open Settings, Commerce, Reviews. Approve reviews before they show is on by default. Untick it to show reviews as soon as they are sent.

Only buyers can review is on by default, so only customers who paid for a product can review it. Untick it to let any signed-in customer review, and their reviews are not marked as verified purchases.
Tick Ask buyers for reviews, and choose the Days after paying, such as fourteen. Each buyer then gets one email with a link to review each product they bought, once it has arrived and been used.
Only buyers who agreed to news and offers are asked, and only for recent orders. This needs your site's email and its base URL, and the Customers module.

chapters.title: Ratings in listings
chapters.subtitle: Sort and filter by customer rating

steps.text: Once a product has an approved review, shoppers can sort a listing by Customer rating, highest first, and the best rated products come to the top.
A listing that chooses its filters automatically also offers a Customer rating filter, such as four and up, three and up and two and up.
To add them to a listing that has its own filters and sorts, edit the listing, open Choose filters, and tick Customer rating. Choose sorts does the same for the sort.

chapters.title: Use cases
chapters.subtitle: How stores put it to work

steps.text: A shop with many similar products: shoppers sort by customer rating and start with the best.
A store that wants honest feedback: leave Only buyers can review on, so every review comes from a real customer.
A busy store: ask buyers for reviews by email a couple of weeks after they pay, so reviews arrive without anyone chasing them.
A brand that guards its name: keep approval on, and reject spam and abuse before anyone sees it.
Product reviews turn what your buyers think into proof, under your control. Thanks for watching.
